data.title: Interferons (systemic, intralesional, topical)
data.summary: Antivirals & ART · Cytokine immunomodulators — IFN-α (2a, 2b, pegylated), IFN-β, IFN-γ (1b); recombinant proteins
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antivirals & ART_

**Class:** Cytokine immunomodulators — IFN-α (2a, 2b, pegylated), IFN-β, IFN-γ (1b); recombinant proteins

## Mechanism of action
- Bind interferon receptors → JAK-STAT signalling → hundreds of interferon-stimulated genes
- Antiviral: inhibit viral replication (2',5'-oligoadenylate synthetase, protein kinase R)
- Antiproliferative and immunomodulatory: activate NK cells, cytotoxic T cells and macrophages, increase MHC expression; IFN-γ activates macrophage killing

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Intralesional IFN-α2b: condylomata acuminata (refractory), keloids (after excision), BCC and SCC (selected), keratoacanthoma, common warts
- Systemic IFN-α: cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides, Sézary — often with PUVA/retinoids), Kaposi sarcoma, melanoma (adjuvant — historical), Behçet disease, chronic hepatitis B/C (historical), life-threatening infantile haemangioma (historical — spastic diplegia risk)
- IFN-γ-1b: chronic granulomatous disease (reduces infections — approved), severe atopic dermatitis (limited), osteopetrosis
- Topical IFN gel/cream: genital warts, herpes (limited)

## Dose & formulations
- Intralesional IFN-α2b for genital warts: 1 million IU into each wart (up to 5 warts) three times a week for 3 weeks
- Systemic IFN-α for CTCL: 3–9 million IU SC three times weekly
- IFN-γ-1b (CGD): 50 µg/m² SC three times weekly

## Adverse effects
- Flu-like syndrome (fever, chills, myalgia, headache) — premedicate with paracetamol; tachyphylaxis over weeks
- Fatigue, depression and suicidal ideation, cognitive changes
- Cytopenias, raised LFT, thyroid dysfunction (hypo/hyper), autoimmunity
- Skin: injection-site reactions/necrosis, alopecia, induction or flare of psoriasis, sarcoidosis, lichen planus, vitiligo, lupus

## Contraindications
- Severe depression or suicidal history; autoimmune hepatitis; decompensated liver disease; uncontrolled thyroid disease; pregnancy (relative)

## Drug interactions
- Theophylline levels rise; additive marrow suppression with zidovudine and other myelosuppressives

## Monitoring
- CBC, LFT, TSH, mood assessment during systemic use

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (abortifacient in animals at high doses).

## Viva points
- IL IFN-α2b for genital warts — 1 MIU per wart thrice weekly × 3 weeks
- IFN-γ for chronic granulomatous disease
- IFN therapy can induce psoriasis and sarcoidosis
- Flu-like illness and depression are the key side effects

_Sources: Khopkar ch.3, ch.13 (Immunobiologicals — interferons) and ch.20 (topical/intralesional IFN); Wolverton 4e ch.43 and ch.37. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
